articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Long Short-Term Memory Through Unlearning-Relearning Soil Quality Parameters Data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Time series prediction, speech recognition, natural language processing, and other sequence-based applications have all shown the benefits of using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. Nevertheless, LSTM models frequently encounter irrelevant input in numerous real-world applications, which lowers prediction accuracy. To improve prediction accuracy, we suggest a novel modification to the LSTM algorithm in this research study. This modification involves dynamically unlearning irrelevant data and relearning relevant data during training. By introducing a mechanism to recognize and adjust the weight of training data, our technique helps the model focus more on relevant data while reducing the impact of irrelevant data. We demonstrate significant improvements in prediction accuracy across a range of tasks and datasets as we illustrate the effectiveness of our improved LSTM.

articleTitle: Unraveling the Enigma of the 2022 Cianjur Earthquake: Insights from Gravity Satellite Data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The 2022 Cianjur Earthquake serves as a stark reminder of the omnipresence of active faults. Despite its moderate magnitude of M5.6 and its distance from the well-known Cimandiri Fault, this earthquake resulted in over 600 fatalities and substantial damage. It presented an unusual challenge, lacking the strength to induce surface rupture or deformation yet causing remarkably intense shaking and scattered building damage. This study employs gravity satellite data, specifically TOPEX data, to explore subsurface anomalies tied to geological structures within the earthquake-affected region. Through mapping, we identify gravity anomalies associated with geological features, active faults, and volcanoes. Our analysis incorporates aftershock distribution, overlaid with a Forest and Building Removed Digital Elevation Model, and geological mapping. Our findings reveal the earthquake's hypocenter positioned amidst gravity anomalies of varying magnitudes. Additionally, we observe that aftershocks are concentrated between two hills of an ancient quaternary volcano, forming a fan-like pattern. Historical earthquake and volcano eruption databases are consulted to assess the potential triggering of volcano flank collapses by past earthquakes. Notably, we detect minor structures suggestive of surface rupture near the landslide-prone area, offering a pivotal location for future investigations into subsurface active faults. For advanced studies, we recommend detailed gravity measurements to enhance structural analysis and understand the subterranean configuration near the earthquake epicenter. Additionally, methods such as electrical resistivity tomography and ground-penetrating radar should be considered. In conclusion, our research underscores the value of an integrated approach, encompassing geophysics, geology, and remote sensing, for comprehensive earthquake studies in this region.

articleTitle: A Monitoring System Carbon Emissions Based on Land in Riau Province
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: This report summarizes most of the progress made in monitoring carbon emissions from land-based sources in the previous year. The complicated dynamics of carbon dynamics caused by human activities such as land-use changes, agriculture, and deforestation have become apparent owing to regular monitoring. The webgis calculated land-based carbon emissions for Riau Province. The webgis monitoring system monitored the land cover, peatland, and carbon stock. In the peatland, Bengkalis, Indragiri Hilir, Indragiri hulu, Kepulauan Meranti, and Siak have the highest rates, at 48.288%. There is a large difference between them and Rokan Hilir District (48.02%) and Pelalawan District (48.08%). Also, in this monitoring system Pelalawan has the largest carbon stock and Kampar has the lowest carbon stock. The abstract emphasizes the importance of continuing to research, develop, and collaborate on a global scale to attain sustainable practices and a healthy world for current and future generations.

articleTitle: Distribution of Carbon Monoxide (CO) According to Industrial Area in West Java 2022
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Remote sensing can be used to monitoring air pollution. The Sentinel 5P satellite has a TROPOMI sensor specifically used to detect pollutant. The Sentinel-5P satellite can detect pollutants on a global scale. One type of pollutant that causes air pollution is Carbon Monoxide (CO). Carbon monoxide comes from incomplete combustion of fuel and organic compounds. The increase in air pollution continues to increase in line with industrial development and the increasing number of motorized vehicles. West Java Province is a province with a large number of industries 20 industrial area. The largest number of industries are in Sumedang, Purwakarta, Bogor, Bekasi, Karawang. The distribution of CO in West Java can be done by processing Sentinel 5P data using Google Earth Engine. In the processing process, the median function is used because it can reduce outlier values in the image. The data used is median monthly CO data in 2022. High CO concentrations are in the northern region of West Java, this is influenced by the presence of industrial areas. The highest CO value was in Bekasi City with a value of 0.047 mol/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>and the lowest value was in South Garut and Garut with a value of 0.023 mol/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The Marunda Center Industrial Area has the highest CO value of 0.041 mol/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>which is the petrochemical industry.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Flood Early Warning System For Remote Deployment and an Integrated Social Media
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Floods are natural disasters that often occur in Indonesia. It is including in the city of Surabaya which still has 117 flood-prone areas. Flood disasters have significant adverse effects on society, which emphasizes the need for an Early Warning System. Existing EWS, however, faces challenges in data processing efficiency, lacks integration with social media, and cannot operate in areas without electricity. This research aims to enhance the reliability of the EWS by optimizing data processing efficiency using the Internet of Things (IoT), integrating seamlessly with social media, and employing renewable energy sources. The proposed Flood utilizes the advantages of the IoT for collecting and analyzing flood-related data. The result shows this scheme enables real-time monitoring and data-driven decision-making. Results also show the system integrates with social media platforms such as Twitter and Telegram, serving as a vital link to the Surabaya community. In consideration of remote deployment challenges, results show that the proposed system has an integrated solar panel energy system to address the issues associated with remote deployment. The system's independence from traditional electrical grids is guaranteed by this environmentally beneficial energy source, which also makes it especially appropriate for deployment in isolated locations with restricted access to electricity. The synergy of IoT, social media, and solar panels in the proposed EWS anticipates a comprehensive approach to flood management, benefiting the Surabaya community by fostering resilience and reducing the vulnerability to flood-related hazards.

articleTitle: Field Survey of Paleotsunami in Bengkulu
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Bengkulu is one of the provinces in Sumatra that is directly facing a subduction zone. This situation causes this area is prone to tsunami disasters. As this province continues to develop, the risk of tsunami hazard is getting higher. The historical record of tsunamis in Bengkulu is still relatively short and inadequate for tsunami mitigation. There has been no previous paleotsunami research in this area. To extend historical record of past tsunamis from a geological perspective in Bengkulu Province, we conducted a paleotsunami survey to reveal the unrecorded past tsunamis in this area. The methods used in this research include coring using a hand auger and observing outcrops by making geological trenches. A total of 20 locations along the coast of Bengkulu Province were surveyed, and selected samples were collected for further laboratory research. Paleotsunami candidate was identified in Kungkai Baru, Seluma. The candidate was observed continuously in several cores at a depth of around 1.2m. It's white sand 2-4cm thick which contains lots of shell fragments and foraminifera deposited in the peat clay layer. Another candidate for paleotsunami layer was identified in the Nusa Indah area of Bangkulu City. This candidate was observed in peat to clay layers at a depth of around 1.9 to 2.5m. As the first paleotsunami study in Bengkulu, the results of this study will be very important not only in the context of tsunami geology research but also for tsunami mitigation.

articleTitle: A Multi-Index Satellite Data Investigation for Corn Growth Patterns Identification
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: This discourse commences with the acknowledgment of the widespread utilization of satellite data and the availability of various vegetation indices for vegetation identification. The Landsat-8 satellite imagery is specifically employed for the analysis discussed herein. The focus is on the rationality of choosing vegetation indices, such as NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index) and NDMI (Normalized Difference Moisture Index), in contrast to the Wetness Index, for monitoring the growth of corn plants over time. Throughout different growth phases, from the initial planting to maturity, the distinctive patterns exhibited by NDWI and NDMI underscore their effectiveness in capturing crucial information related to plant and soil moisture content. The contextual preference for NDWI and NDMI over the Wetness Index is emphasized, showcasing their relevance in precision agriculture practices and their contribution to informed decision-making for optimal corn crop management.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Tilt Derivative (TDR) and Second Vertical Derivative (SVD) from Gravity Data, Case Study: Umbul Niti Geothermal Field
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The gravity method is a passive technique measures the response of rock or mineral's density which correspond to the gravity acceleration. In this study, we use gravity data acquired from a potential geothermal area in Umbul Niti, South Lampung. Analyzing geothermal systems involves examining components such as the heat source, reservoir, clay cap, and faults. This study places particular emphasis on the identification of subsurface faults as pathways for the recharge and discharge of geothermal systems, utilizing gravity data. One of the important steps in processing gravity data is anomaly enhancement. In this research, a comparative study of Tilt Derivative (TDR) and Second Vertical Derivative (SVD) filters was performed to infer the subsurface fault. Synthetic gravity data are needed to check the boundary of low and dense material using TDR and SVD analysis. The synthetic data show that the border of the body anomaly is located at the zero contour of the TDR and SVD map. Thus, the estimated subsurface faults were revealed from the zero contour of the TDR and SVD. The application of TDR and SVD to the gravity field data exhibits that the majority of subsurface faults trend provide Northwest - Southeast directions. Hence, the estimation of subsurface faults is indicative of the continuity of the Lampung Panjang Fault.

articleTitle: Design of a Real-Time Tracking and Telemetry Parsing System for S-band Satellites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The number of satellites being launched every year is increasing, with several academic institutes too taking part in designing satellites and payloads for satellites. A ground station is needed to receive and transmit signals, to and from satellites. The uplink data from ground station to satellite is mostly Telecommand and the downlink data is either Telemetry or Payload. Telemetry data provides information related to the health and essential parameters of the satellite with Payload data focusing on the data related to major application of the satellite. In this paper, an attempt is made to design an inhouse real-time tracking and telemetry parsing system for an S-band satellite named SindhuNetra, designed by PES University, along with RCI-DRDO and launched by ISRO. The proposed work is carried out using a ground station with Sband antenna commissioned at PES University and Software Defined Radio module. A graphical user interface is also developed using Python scripts and other open source software to monitor the telemetry data in real-time. Three models are explored for the proposed work with the maximum Figure of Merit (FOM) obtained being 0.996 with an average FOM of 0.92. The proposed work will benefit academic institutes launching satellites to track and monitor their satellite using proposed ground station.

articleTitle: Volume Calculation Accuracy and 3D Visualization of Flexible Pavement Damage Based on Low-cost LiDAR
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Identification of the current condition of road infrastructure still requires high and long survey costs and time. The development of the digital revolution changed the survey pattern for assessing road damage conditions. Unfortunately, the available technology is expensive and requires operators and unique expertise. The development of smartphones with LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) technology opens up new avenues for low-cost scanning applications. This study compares two smartphone devices with LiDAR sensor technology for their 3d viewing capabilities and accuracy in measuring road damage volume. This study uses a spot and continuous scan for the data collecting method. The spot scan method involves scanning the data in a fixed position parallel to the observation object. The continuous scan method gathers data by walking over an observation object simultaneously. The results showed that both devices could produce 3-D visualization; However, the image quality of the result was inadequate, and it could provide an image of objects in their initial states. The spot scan approach yields highly precise volume calculation, with an average error of 1.25%. Meanwhile, volumetric measurement based on continuous analysis gave suboptimal results with an error of 11.82%. The two low-cost LiDAR devices can offer a novel, economical, and time-saving alternative to the survey approach for assessing flexible pavement damage identification with the correct scanning method.

articleTitle: Air Quality Monitoring in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Designing air quality monitoring systems is a current trend and topic of study. The sheer number of automobiles entering cities adds to poor air quality and growing levels of air pollution, both of which have major health repercussions. The development was done for air quality parameters using eight criteria: carbon monoxide (CO), formaldehyde (HCHO), methane (CH4), ozone (O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>), nitrogen dioxide (NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), sulfur dioxide (SO2), cloud cover, and the aerosol index. These parameters are derived from the satellite Sentinel 5P imagery in early 2019 till now. We can find ground-level ozone, the gases burned, fuels, industrial areas, and corona disease detection. This can be investigated using the Google Earth Engine (GEE). For CO and O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> concentrations is relative range at 0.016 to 0.0608 and 0.1076 to 0.121 and the aerosol is in medium level concentration. This application may be used to investigate the environment and make decisions.

articleTitle: Redefining Rescue: UAVs and Advanced Algorithms for Life Sign Detection Post-Disasters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Natural disasters are natural events that have a major impact on humans that come suddenly, anywhere, to anyone and cannot be avoided by anyone. Indonesia is a country that has a high level of vulnerability to natural disasters. One of the natural disasters that often hit Indonesia are earthquakes, tsunamis, volcanic eruptions, floods, droughts, hurricanes, landslides, and others. The location and time of occurrence of natural disasters that cannot be predicted by humans which then has the potential to take many lives. The fast and precise handling of arrests by the SAR (search and rescue) team is one of the efforts to reduce the number of people who lose their lives. But in reality, the SAR team experienced problems during the process of taking victims. Starting from terrain that is difficult to reach to the limited equipment needed. One solution to the problems that occur due to delays in post-disaster handling is to develop tools that can assist the identification process so that it can facilitate the search for victims after a natural disaster. In this study implemented a system to be able to detect victims of natural disasters which aims to help develop equipment for the SAR team to find victims of natural disasters based on image processing. Image processing is intended to detect whether victims of natural disasters are still alive or not. The algorithm used to detect whether or not there are victims uses the You Only Look Once (YOLO) version 5 method which has a high enough value of 90.75<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> to be able to detect human objects. After being detected by humans, the system will continue the live or dead detection through the specified skeleton point using Tensorflow MoveNet with 100% accuracy from the 14 videos tried.

articleTitle: Affordability of Health Services for Cancer Patients in Mojokerto Area
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The quality of health facilities is very important in providing quality health services to the community. Healthcare facilities are important to provide health services to the community, which is important to improve modern society's quality of life and social welfare. The government has an obligation to provide adequate and quality health facilities to ensure equitable distribution of health services, including equitable distribution of health facilities and accessibility in terms of location. The study using Network Analysis was conducted to determine the accessibility of health facilities in each region in Mojokerto to reach Dr. Wahidin Sudiro Husodo Mojokerto Hospital and/or other facilities that have the same services as Mojokerto Hospital. Based on the results of network analysis, it is known that the range of services and travel time needed to reach Dr. Wahidin Sudiro Husodo Hospital, cancer patients in the Mojokerto area require an increase in quantity. This improvement is expected to divide the service area with easier coverage and shorter handling time. This study uses the network analysis method to determine the affordability of health facility services in each sub-district, to go to Dr. Wahidin Sudiro Husodo Mojokerto Hospital and/or other facilities that have the same order as Dr. Wahidin Sudiro Husodo Mojokerto Hospital. Based on the results of Network Analysis measurements, it was found that the range of services and travel time needed to reach hospitals with cancer facilities in the Mojokerto area requires an increase in quantity. This additional quantity is expected to divide the service area with easier coverage and shorter handling time.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Accuracy Using Post-Processing Kinematic (PPK) Method for Measuring the Situation of Open Pit Mining in PT. Berau Coal
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Mining sector plays a significant role in the national economy and development, as a major contributor to the country's foreign exchange. Technological advancements in surveying offer another alternative for mining survey measurements, specifically using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U$</tex> nmanned Aerial Vehicles (UA V). UA V represent the latest technological development that has been proven to be an efficient and highly accurate alternative for topographic measurements. In this study, a comparison was conducted on the correction of aerial photo results using UAV in Site Gurimbang Mine Operation PT. Berau Coal Energy. We are employing the Post Processing Kinematic (PPK) method with and without Ground Control Points (GCPs). The results of the PPK correction with GCPs show smaller errors. We check the accuracy our analysis using the SNI 8202–2019 standard for Basic Map Accuracy. We also compared the volume between the data acquired from UA V acquisition and Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) data, resulting in a standard deviation of 0.38%. This deviation is consistent with the ASTM standard, which is 2%.

articleTitle: Mapping and Characterization of Seamounts in the Flores Sea Using Acoustic Remote Sensing and Gravity Core Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: This study employs underwater acoustic remote sensing technology and deep-sea soil sampling to map and characterize the seafloor in the Flores Sea to examine the seamounts and potential deposits. The Multibeam Echosounder (MBES) is utilized as an underwater acoustic remote sensing instrument to provide high-resolution ocean bathymetry data, while the gravity core technology collects sediment data in the deep sea. Considering the geological and bathymetric background of the Flores Sea, tectonic processes may have contributed to seamount formation. Seamounts offer geological conditions conducive to mineralization. Thus, the study aims to map seamounts and assess their mineralization potential in the Flores Sea. Caris HIPS SIPS software is utilized to process the MBES data, while sediment analysis uses the megascopically technique. These data are qualitatively used to characterize seafloor features and identify mineralization indicators and ultimately will enhance our understanding of seamounts and their mineralization potential. The study has successfully identified a new seamount in the Flores Sea, located 120 km north of Mount Tambora, along with the presence of mineralization. These findings are expected to significantly contribute to resource mapping. Moreover, it could improve insights into seamounts and mineralization will aid further exploration and research in marine geology.

articleTitle: Improving the Effectiveness of Remote Sensing Data Correction Using Phase Cross-Correlation Algorithm with Upsampling Factors Variable
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Geometric accuracy is one of the problems in using satellite imagery and geometry correction is a necessary step before using the imagery for various applications and analysis. Image-to-image registration is one of the geometric correction methods that can be easily used to find the shifted pixel in satellite imagery. This paper specifically analyzes the phase cross-correlation method implemented in two images with different acquisition times. The goal of this research is to find the impacts of the upsampling factor by adjusting its variable in order to improve its effectiveness in terms of fixing distorted images. Using a study area in Pacitan Regency, two highresolution photos of Pleiades are divided into four polygons, each with four bands. In each band of polygons, the upsampling factor variables are applied sequentially on a scale of 10 - 10.000 to discover the relation between its effectiveness and processing time. The result shows that the higher the upsampling factor, the greater the sub-pixel precision and vice versa. At some point, the greater processing time does not outweigh the higher accuracy. This paper found that the best upsampling factor is 1000 with accuracy up to three digits after decimal points and a processing time of less than 23 seconds. Finding the precise upsampling value can simplify the geometric correction process with image registration. Determining the precise upsampling value will be very helpful for remote sensing data users to carry out the correction process, the highest sub-pixel precision can be achieved with equitable processing time.

articleTitle: PBIM: A Patch-Based Image Mosaicking for UAV Images with Natural Scene Distortions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The process of creating a seamless mosaic from a set of UAV-acquired images involves aligning and blending individual images to produce a coherent and comprehensive representation of the surveyed area. However, images captured by drones often suffer from distortion, specifically caused by the complex interaction between the camera sensor, lens, and the three-dimensional scene-referred to as natural scene distortion. These distortions significantly impact the overall visual quality of the generated UAV mosaic. While this problem has been extensively studied in the context of conventional photography, it has received less attention in the context of UAV -based images. The purpose of this study is to develop a less complex solution comprising two components: 1) patch-based image mosaicking (PBIM) and 2) CNN-based distortion detection and classification via transfer learning. The patch-based image mosaicking outperformed other existing software solutions in terms of creating a comprehensive visualization of the UAV mosaic. On the other hand, the CNN-based component identified the best model with a pre-trained VGGNet network, achieving a highest accuracy of 65.59% in detection and classification, as well as an average of 10.25 in the generation of sub-directories for data aggregation across the entire test dataset. The PIQE evaluation metric indicated that the majority of the U A V mosaics produced using the proposed solution exhibited good quality. Furthermore, when assessed using the background proportion metric introduced in this study, the proposed method produced the best overall visual appearance quality compared to other solutions.

articleTitle: Comparing Online Destination Images of Southeast Asia MICE Destinations Projected through the Website of the Convention and Visitors Bureau
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: In the current competitive landscape, promoting the image of a MICE destination through the Convention and Visitor Bureau (CVB) website is imperative. The primary goals of such activity in particular are to enhance the destination image and to attract the presence of various MICE events at the destination. Numerous studies show that visual elements projected through an online platform, such as a website, can have a significant impact on the image of a destination. However, such a study has never been conducted in the setting of CVB websites, particularly in the context of Southeast Asia destinations that compete with one another and share relatively similar destination attributes. The main purpose of this study is to identify and compare the different image categories projected by the CVB official websites within the context of three major MICE destinations in Southeast Asia (Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand). In doing so, this research use a free image downloader application (Imageye) which enables us to download all the images on a particular website. After that we also applied two data collection methods sequentially, namely visual content analysis and correspondence analysis. This study suggests that there are differences in destination image categories projected online through their CVB websites. Moreover, other conclusions for research and practice are also formulated.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an Integrated Data Processing Unit with Range Matched Filtering for Lab Scale Synthetic Aperture Radar Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The Indonesian National Research and Innovation Agency (BRIN) is currently developing a synthetic aperture radar sensor for a medium-altitude, long endurance aircraft platform for remote sensing applications. The first lab-scale version of the developed SAR system consists of three main parts: transmitter and receiver antennas, an RF subsystem, and a data processing module. The antennas are linearly polarized, and the RF uses a chirp pulsed wave with a 5.3 GHz center frequency and a 150 MHz bandwidth, aiming for 1 m spatial range resolution. The ADC module of the Data Acquisition Unit (DAU) sampled the received baseband IQ signal from the receiver module and saved the complex value into secondary storage, which was then transferred for offline processing. In this paper, we present the implementation of integration between the DAU and the Data Processing Unit (DPU) to optimize signal processing time. With the new design, the current data processing steps can be reduced so that the required time can also be shortened. This will be very useful, especially in field experiments. The design and implementation of a range-matched filtering module as a part of DPU are presented and tested with outdoor SAR experiment data.

articleTitle: Earthquake Hazard Modeling in Java Using Space Time Epidemic Type Aftershock Sequence
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Appropriate earthquake hazard modeling is important for Indonesia to produce a more accurate earthquake hazard map because Indonesia is one of the most vulnerable countries for earthquake occurrence, especially Java region which is considered as the most populated region. However, previous study cannot perform analysis for complete earthquake catalog data in Indonesia because it requires complex model with a number of parameters and computationally expensive approach. In this study, we perform earthquake analysis using the space-time epidemic type aftershock sequence (space-time ETAS) in Java occurred during 1 January 2003 to 30 June 2023 with magnitude greater than 4 and depth less than 300 km. We consider the combination of Davidon-Fletcher-Powell and stochastic declustering algorithms to obtain a scalable procedure. The results show that Java has a low earthquake rate, i.e. less than 0.1 events/day.deg2, and a moderate clustering coefficient. This research provides information that the number of earthquakes in Java is relatively small and is not significantly influenced by the occurrence time of the main earthquake.

articleTitle: Determining the Impact of a Dam on the Natural Hydro-Sedimentary Dynamics Using Remote Sensing and GIS: Case of the Hassan Ad-Dakhil Dam (South-East Morocco)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The construction of dams has significantly altered natural hydro-sedimentary dynamics, raising concerns about their environmental impacts. In response, this study proposes an integrated geomatics approach to determine the impact of a dam on the natural hydro-sedimentary dynamics through the estimation of the annual sediment rate trapped in a dam using two complementary formulas, which are simultaneously applied for the first time. The initial equation assesses hydrological erosion occurring upstream of the dam, providing an estimation of the annual erosion-susceptible soil rate within the dam's watershed. This assessment leverages the integration of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and Remote Sensing technologies with the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE). The subsequent equation proposed by Williams (1977), computes the sediment delivery ratio, facilitating the estimation of sediment transportation rate towards the dam's reservoir through overland flows. The validation of the estimated annual sediment rate trapped in the dam is done by comparing it to the measured rate. The pilot case of this study is the Hassan Ad-Dakhil dam in South-East Morocco. Remote sensing data, a digital elevation model, precipitation, and pedological data were used for hydrological modeling of the dam's watershed associated to the Ziz River. The results include maps showing factors influencing hydrological erosion, the rate of lands sensitive to erosion, sediment delivery ratio, and the annual rate of lands trapped in the reservoir. This approach could enable biologists to simulate disturbances in downstream aquatic ecosystems caused by dams and hydrologists to estimate the dam's lifespan without dredging during dry months.

articleTitle: CustodyChainGuardian: Blockchain of Custody Digital Evidence Preservation System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Digital forensic investigation is a systematic process for identifying, preserving, collecting, analyzing, and presenting digital evidence in court. Chain-of-custody (CoC) is crucial, ensuring the evidence's integrity and admissibility. Blockchain technology, with its characteristics of openness, decentralization, and immutable ledger, offers enhanced security and transparency for maintaining digital evidence during forensic investigations. This paper presents the CustodyChainGuardian (CCG) framework, a multi-layered methodology designed to ensure the integrity, authenticity, and traceability of digital evidence throughout its lifecycle. The four-layer architecture includes the Front-end Layer, Cloud Layer, Database Layer, and Blockchain Layer. The Front-end Layer provides a user-friendly interface for evidence submission and management, while the Cloud Layer offers robust storage and backup capabilities. The Database Layer stores original digital evidence with unique identifiers and strict access control. The Blockchain Layer introduces immutability and transparency to the chain-of-custody. Rigorous experimentation validates the system's effectiveness and reliability.

articleTitle: Monitoring of Land Use Changes Using Google Earth Engine for Agriculture: Indramayu Regency
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Indramayu is pivotal for national food security, acting as a buffer with designated sustainable agricultural land. Amidst industrial development in the Rebana Area, including six Industrial Designated Areas, potential threats to sustainable agricultural land arise from land conversion. This study utilizes big spatial data and machine learning on time-series satellite imagery to analyze past, current, and future prediction analyses. The data used are sentinel-2 imagery and NDVI, NDWI, and BSI index derivatives. Using Google Earth Engine (GEE), a dashboard is created to visualize, create, and store datasets, and the dataset results will be classified for land use and land cover (LULC) using the Random Forest algorithm. On the GEE dashboard, a dataset was efficiently generated through the implementation of several processes: timing window selection, cloud filtering, spectral index calculation, imagery integration, and classification. The classification result shows that the best model for Sentinel-2 in Indramayu Regency uses random forest pixel-based analysis compared to object-based analysis. Using GEE, monitoring LULC changes can support Indramayu's vision to see the potential and prospect of a national food reserve, contributing to informed agricultural development decisions for enhanced food security.

articleTitle: Mapping Urban Income Pattern Via Geospatial - Based Expert Opinion Technique in Selangor Malaysia
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: This paper focuses on urban income mapping with a proposed technique of geospatial-based expert opinion in Section 8 Kota Damansara, Selangor. The study aims to estimate and map income status and patterns, especially in urban areas. A GIS database and based mapping of the income were created using spatial digitising and satellite imagery extraction. The secondary gross income data and an experienced expert opinion from Petaling Jaya City Council (PJCC) were obtained to provide the community income estimation and scenario. While datasets from the Social Housing or People's Housing Programme (PPR) and site visit observations were applied to support the estimated income results, The key finding revealed that the income status map and database were quickly updated compared to the existing map approach, providing significant benefits to the PJCC in understanding the socio-economic status of the Section community. The income map with dark red colours represents the lowest gross household income, which is mostly occupied by the PPR community. The study also found that the lower-income group has been most affected by employment and income losses. The GIS-based expert opinion income map has provided a holistic view of the local population, categorised into top-to-bottom income status. This alternative framework could be used for digital income geodatabases and geo-mapping as a cost-effective and time-saving technique.

articleTitle: Preserving Historical Significance: HBIM Implementation for The East Hall of Bandung Institute of Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: This research proposes and implements the HBIM model for the ITB East Hall. The HBIM approach combines BIM principles with the unique needs associated with preserving historic buildings. Through detailed mapping and modeling of the building, architectural elements, and building characteristics, HBIM enabled the creation of an accurate and rich digital representation of the physical condition and history of the East Hall. The research methodology involves 3D scanning mapping using the latest laser scanning technology to obtain precise geometric data. The data is then integrated into a BIM software environment, where a three-dimensional building model is generated. Additional information, such as historical changes, materials, and historical construction methods, is also integrated into the HBIM model. This research results in an HBIM model that provides a holistic and accurate digital representation of the ITB East Hall. These models can serve as an important source of information for building preservation, maintenance, and management purposes. HBIM models can also be a valuable educational tool, allowing users to interactively explore the history and architectural complexity of buildings. By applying the HBIM approach to the ITB East Hall, this research provides a real example of how BIM technology can be adapted to preserve cultural heritage buildings. This opens opportunities for similar applications in other cultural heritage buildings, bridging the gap between modern technology and valuable cultural heritage.

articleTitle: Systematic Geometric Correction Method of Stereo Image Data Proposes for the Next Indonesian Satellite
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Indonesia, facing a high susceptibility to natural disasters, has embarked on the development of its Earth observation satellites, ranging from LAPAN-A1 to the upcoming LAPAN-A4 (tentative name). Given the nation's need for disaster mitigation tools, the forthcoming satellite generation aims to generate stereo image data. Such data is instrumental in constructing Digital Surface Models (DSMs), providing insights into Earth's surface shape for modeling disasters like floods, land subsidence, and landslides. The precision of the resulting DSM relies on the image matching algorithm and image orientation, influenced by the sensor model. Two prevalent sensor models, the physical or rigorous model and the generalized model, govern imaging geometry. Notably, the Rational Function Model (RFM) has gained prominence among generalized models due to its superior accuracy compared to rigorous counterparts. This paper delves into the study and proposal of a generalized sensor model for the application to stereo optical image data from the line scan imager (pushbroom) of the next generation of Indonesian satellites.

articleTitle: Optimum System Design for Performance Monitoring of Buildings under Seismic Excitation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Monitoring the vibration behavior of buildings during and after an earthquake requires sensors installed in the buildings. Buildings installed with these sensors will transmit data to a monitoring center so that the stakeholders are provided with information on the performance of the buildings during the earthquake and whether the building is still safe or not after the earthquake. This paper discusses the development of optimum sensor systems capable of providing data for the above purposes.

articleTitle: An AHP-based GIS method to detect biotic and abiotic stress factors of a Cacao Farm in Cebu, Philippines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Cacao (Theobroma cacao L.) is widely cultivated in the cacao belt-l0 to 20 degrees north and south of the equator-where the Philippines is situated. Nonetheless, the country suffers from low cacao yield and imports cacao products. The country's cacao roadmap for 2017–2022 identified environmental stress factors such as light intensity, relative humidity, temperature, rainfall, soil quality, flooding, shade, and insect pests and diseases. Conventionally, cacao farmers apply the ground survey method in detecting stress factors, which is prone to human error. This study assessed a cacao farm's stress level through its top environmental stress factors by applying an advanced monitoring system. A combination of the hierarchical modeling in AHP and the GIS method is applied on a specific five-hectare cacao farm to manage the decreasing cacao production. The area boundary was extracted through drone mapping and using an AHP pairwise matrix for an expert ranking of the identified stress factors. In addition, a Sentinel-2 image was used to calculate the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) to classify identified areas as healthy, stressed, and very stressed. The NDVI map showed that Zone 3 has the highest average stress level among the four zones. The top five stress factors are insect pests and diseases, floods, soil quality, temperature, and rainfall. Policy implications are derived from these results to mitigate the effects of these stress factors.

articleTitle: Exploring Regional Dynamics Through Social Media Conversations and Socio-Economic Surveys: Uncovering Perspectives on the Cianjur Earthquake
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The seismic event of magnitude 5.6 in Cianjur, West Java, in November 2022 had severe consequences, causing loss of lives, extensive infrastructure damage, and lasting socio-economic challenges. This research investigates the psychosocial aspects of the community's response, particularly sentiments toward the post-earthquake scenario. Combining field surveys and social media analysis, the study employs a text mining framework to develop a sentiment model. The research question focuses on the specifications and insights derived from the sentiment model regarding the aftermath of the earthquake disaster in Cianjur. Various classification algorithms are tested, with the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) Algorithm proving superior with an F1 score of 87%. Application of the model to the dataset reveals a slightly higher prevalence of negative sentiment (53.50<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) compared to positive sentiment (46.50<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>). Discrepancies with survey data highlight nuanced perspectives, influenced by factors such as disagreement on relocation, cost concerns for earthquake-resistant housing, and issues related to illicit activities. Social media discussions also reveal insights into public satisfaction with government assistance and challenges in rebuilding homes. The study identifies additional factors influencing sentiment results, including model specifications, inaccuracies in perceptions, and emotional factors, contributing valuable insights for disaster response planning, policy evaluation, and targeted interventions. Overall, this research enhances understanding of community sentiments post-disaster by integrating perspectives from traditional surveys and dynamic social media conversations.

articleTitle: Impact of Oil Injection on Concentrations of Chlorophyll, Carotenoids, Anthocyanins in Banyan Leaves and Ketapang Dewa Leaves Using Hyperspectral Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Oil leaks can occur in pipes that have been used for a long time, leading to small leaks in the pipes. The oil seeps into the soil where the plant roots are. Continuous oil seepage can affect the growth of plants around it. The research in this paper focuses on the phenomenon of oil seepage in shade trees that have many leaves and can provide shade, specifically the Banyan tree (B) or ficus benjamina and the Ketapang Dewa tree (KD) or terminalia catappa. Plants were infused with 5 ml, 10 ml, and 15 ml of oil, once a day for 8 weeks. Observe the impact of the oil leak observed with the hyperspectral sensor through the leaves of each Banyan tree (B) and Ketapang Dewa (KD) leaves to determine the chlorophyll concentration value greens, anthocyanins, and carotenes. As a result of this study, from the Hyperspectral sensor, (KD) reflectance data showed an increase of 0.44 for 10ml oil penetration and 0.20 for 5ml oil penetration with a wavelength of 551nm.

articleTitle: Decoding Drought: Embracing Simplicity in Effective Predictive Models
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Drought, a recurring environmental challenge, poses severe threats to ecosystems, agriculture, and water resources worldwide, significantly affecting the ecological balance and socioeconomic stability. The state of Rajasthan, with its long history of droughts, faces these issues due to its arid climate and irregular rainfall. This paper presents a comparative analysis of drought prediction models, focusing on the Rajasthan region using two datasets: Vegetation Health Index (VHI) and VHI + Rainfall. The study evaluates six machine learning and deep learning models, including Multivariate Linear Regression (MLR), Random Forest (RF), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Regressor (SVR), and 1-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1DCNN). The integration of two datasets contributes to the study's novelty, with KNN excelling in incorporating both VHI and Rainfall. MLR emerges as a robust choice with the highest average R2 score of 0.944, and lowest average MSE and MAE of 0.004 and 0.033 respectively for the VHI dataset while KNN leads with an average R2 score of 0.928, and least MSE and MAE of 0.005 and 0.036 respectively for VHI + Rainfall dataset. These findings emphasize the potential of simpler models for effective drought prediction.

articleTitle: Mathematical Vibration Model for Attached Camera System for A Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: A mathematical methodology to assess the effects of vibrations on a mobile robot's video system components is being developed and implemented. The robot is a mobile platform for placing specialized equipment for various uses. The vibrations of structural components of multi-bearing wheeled vehicles were examined using mathematical models and empirical data. This study supports the use of a stochastic mathematical model to describe mobile robot vibrations. Under diverse robot motion conditions, the vibration model is a correlation function or spectral density of a stochastic process. To replicate a random vibration process with specified features, shaping filter differential equations are supplied. The vibration process, probabilistic moments, and differential equations are given. The probabilistic moment equations and formula were used to analyze vibration amplitudes exceeding a threshold. Random process emissions indicate how well the mobile platform equipment retains its core properties. An extensive mathematical model was analyzed to estimate stochastic vibration emission intensity. The Probabilistic vibration method and emission intensity properties are determined. Theoretical discoveries allow the evaluation of mobile video system components and the determination of fundamental tolerances. The mathematical framework for assessing vibrations was proven by computer simulation.

articleTitle: Early Aesthetics Integration in Digital Twin Dashboards in Isolated Agriculture: Data Modelling and Remote Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Agricultural enterprises are awakening to the realization of the benefits of digital twins. The rapid integration of dashboard management in remote agricultural locations is driven by the emerging accepted practices involving digital twins. In many cases these amalgamations are limited by agricultural environments that incorporate technology, communication and understand their value in creating optimization, profit, and sustain ability. Many environments are insufficiently mature to benefit from the full impact of digital twin modeling, yet farmers, pastoralists and horticulturalists continue to trial and test different technologies because they seek to replicate their rivals and choose to integrate technology as and when individual elements become available, affordable, and applicable. This paper evaluates dashboard processes by case study comparisons. It discusses the decision-making processes that lead to effective deployment of digital twinning and its benefits and posits the importance of aesthetic feature inclusion on dashboards in remote reporting locations.

articleTitle: Design and Testing of Data Communication System Integration on RX-450.03 Sounding Rocket
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The RX-450 rocket is a ballistic rocket with a diameter of 450mm. It is equipped with avionic sensors such as accelerometers and gyroscopes coupled to a microprocessor, RF systems with frequencies of 900 MHz and 2.4 GHz, and a navigation system/Global Positioning System (GPS). The objective of the research was to build a data communication system that could be attached to the rocket, and then conduct a rocket flight test to identify the characteristics of the rocket dynamics during flight. Based on the data collected, it was observed that the rocket accelerated up to 10g in the 17th second. Additionally, the GPS data was lost at 36.25 Km in the 66<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> second.

articleTitle: Analysis of Rice Productivity Estimation in East Java Province And Its Relationship to Poverty
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Rice remains a significant agricultural commodity, retaining its status as a fundamental dietary staple. This underscores its pivotal role in ensuring both economic and political equilibrium within the Indonesian region. Amidst the spectrum of national economic challenges, poverty takes center stage as a prominent concern confronting the Indonesian populace. The province most acutely affected by this predicament is East J ava, boasting a noteworthy poverty rate. In the year 2022, the poverty headcount in East Java Province escalated to a staggering 4,472.74 million individuals. Intriguingly, East Java Province emerges as a leader in rice productivity for 2022, boasting an impressive 0.562 kg/m2. This insight was gleaned through the utilization of Landsat-8 Level 2 imagery, which facilitated the computation of Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) on paddy fields. The subsequent estimation of rice productivity, accomplished via a regression equation model, yielded an average of 0.567 kg/m2, An alternate methodology involved the employment of the ARIMA forecasting model, drawing upon statistical data spanning 2013 to 2021. This approach yielded an average estimated rice paddy productivity of 0.567 kg/m2, The variance of 4.78<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> between the two methodologies was determined via the Lost Capacity equation. Notably, the percentage of poverty exhibited a correlation with the estimated productivity value, substantiating a noteworthy assertion: heightened productivity corresponds with diminished poverty rates.

articleTitle: Wristband for Elderly Individuals: Esp-32 and Arduino Nano Enabled Solution for Health Monitoring and Tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Effective healthcare monitoring and tracking solutions for senior individuals are urgently needed given the growing geriatric population and rising healthcare expenses. In order to provide a complete healthcare monitoring and tracking wristband for senior people, this research study suggests a wristwatch system using ESP-32 and Arduino N ano microcontrollers. Heart rate monitoring, fall detection, sleepwalk detection, GPS tracking, medication reminders, temperature monitoring, and an emergency SOS button are just a few of the functionalities that the wristband incorporates from a variety of sensors. Caretakers may check on the old person's health from a distance thanks to the technology, which transmits real-time health information to a specialized smartphone app. The technology sends notifications to surrounding caretakers in the event of crises or unstable health metrics. The suggested wristband has the potential to improve older people's quality of life by encouraging preventative care and allowing them to safely age in place. To solve usability and privacy issues, however, more development and user testing are essential. The results of the research indicate that this cutting-edge wristwatch technology has the potential to greatly enhance healthcare outcomes for the senior population.

articleTitle: Urban Evolution Predictions: Cellular Automata-Based Land Cover Change Analysis in Surabaya (2015–2021)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: This study investigates the dynamic transformation of Surabaya's urban environment from 2015 to 2021 by employing satellite imagery and Cellular Automata (CA) simulations to predict alterations in land cover. This study provides essential perspectives for the fields of urban planning and environmental management, emphasizing significant urban expansion and its consequences, thus providing direction for sustainable development approaches in Surabaya. The study centers on critical components such as road networks, rivers, and the Central Business District through the analysis of land cover changes and the prediction of forthcoming shifts utilizing the CA model. The Random Forest algorithm was employed to analyze data obtained from Sentinel-2 satellite imagery on the Google Earth Engine cloud platform. The results indicate that Surabaya witnessed a decline of 40.60% in rice fields (6680.806 hectares) during the period from 2015 to 2021. In contrast, the city witnessed an expansion of 31.98% in buildings (5262.554 hectares) and 21.83% in roads (3592.240 hectares). The utilization of cellular automata to implement Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) to simulate land use change yielded a model that achieved an accuracy of 63.036%, as indicated by a kappa value of 0.49031. Water bodies are the land cover class most prone to change, as indicated by a probability value of 0.369. It is anticipated that structured land cover will predominate by 2030, comprising 57.774% of the total land area or 19373.40 hectares. Furthermore, under Surabaya's RDTR (Detailed Spatial Plan), the projected aggregate land utilization for 2030 is 46.10% (0.461), whereas non-compliant utilization accounts for 53.89% (0.5389).
